lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.17 - A. Complete the travel brochure.

details: Complete the travel brochure helps students to develop their reading and writing skills through using simple pictures and maps to create a travel brochure. It helps build accuracy with vocabulary for attractions and directions.
Look for correct attraction names, clear and simple direction sentences, accurate use of map clues, and neat handwriting.
“Do you think I could be a tour guide? I love talking and writing about famous places! What about you? Could you create your very own brochure? Then let’s vote for our favourite place to visit!

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.17 - B. Listen and write O or X.

details: Listen and write O or X develops listening comprehension skills by having students compare what they hear with visual options.
Look for careful listening, correct responses based on the audiotrack and good comprehension.
“Hmm…I wonder how to get to this attraction? There are so many pictures and ways to go. Can you help me work it  out? Let’s listen together.”

details: Look and write develops reading and writing accuracy by helping students complete simple sentences using visual prompts. It reinforces key vocabulary such as giving directions.
Look for correct sentence completion based on the images shown, accurate use of vocabulary, and neat handwriting.

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.18 - Speaking Look at the places to find.  Ask & answer with your friend and complete the map.

details:
Look at the places to find helps students develop their map-reading skills by asking them to find places on the map. 

Ask and answer helps students with their speaking and listening skills and builds confidence and oral fluency.
Look for creativity, good use of travel vocabulary, accurate responses to the prompts on the map (travel times etc), and students taking turns asking questions and answering them.

“Wow, what great work today! You’ve remembered where to go and how to get there. Now I really want a holiday! Let’s play a Speaking Game to celebrate. Tell your friend what’s on your map. Lead the way!”
